I do not think so.

I do not want you to give up on life.
Still, isn't it a little expensive?
It may certainly feel a bit expensive.

meanings.note: Very polite, deferential form of あなた used by salespeople or service staff.

examples.text: あなた様にお似合いです。
あなた様のご意見をお聞かせください。
examples.trans: Please let us hear your opinion.

meanings.note: Godan verb; in ～ということ, means 'the fact that...' or 'meaning that...'.

examples.text: それはどういうことですか。
田中さんという人が来ました。

meanings.note: Humble counterpart of いる, commonly used in ～ております.
Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Short for かもしれない; expresses possibility or uncertainty.
Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.note: Casual sentence-ending particle.

examples.trans: Well, that's just how it is.

meanings.note: Standard polite 'goodbye'.
Ichidan verb; most commonly appears in the set expression かもしれない ('might be').

examples.text: 遅れるかもしれません。
本当かもしれませんよ。
examples.trans: It might be true, you know.

meanings.en: short casual form of じゃあ / では
meanings.note: Brisk spoken transition before taking the next step.

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.en: whichever (after question word); or something like
meanings.note: After どれ (どれでも) means 'any one at all'; after a noun (店でも) suggests an example ('a shop or something').

examples.text: いつでも来てください。
お茶でも飲みませんか。
examples.trans: Won't you have tea or something?

meanings.note: Conjunctive particle contrasting two things, showing the reality is even more extreme.

examples.text: 休むどころか、もっと忙しくなった。
examples.trans: Far from resting, I got even busier.

examples.text: 高いどころか安すぎます。
examples.trans: Far from being expensive, it's too cheap.

meanings.note: Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

なら.gloss: if it is; in the case of

meanings.note: Conditional topic marker placed right after a noun or pronoun (あなたなら 'if it were you').

examples.text: あなたならどうしますか？
examples.trans: If it were you, what would you do?

examples.text: 明日なら時間があります。
examples.trans: If it is tomorrow, I have time.

meanings.note: Expresses change of state, or in polite customer service (になります) states an arrangement or price total.

examples.trans: That comes to one thousand yen.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Checks agreement ('isn't it?') or softens a request or farewell.
Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.
I-adjective; after て-form (～てほしい), means 'want someone to do something'.

examples.trans: I want you to come soon.

examples.text: 諦めてほしくないのです。
examples.trans: I don't want you to give up.

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.en: do for an inferior (tough-guy てやる)
meanings.note: After て-form (勘弁してやる), expresses granting a favor from a position of authority.

examples.trans: I will give you a hand (casual masculine).

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Between の and な (あなたのような人), describes someone or something 'like ...'.

examples.text: 春のような暖かい日です。
examples.trans: It is a warm day like spring.

examples.text: あなたのような人を探していました。
examples.trans: I was looking for someone like you.

meanings.note: Formal, polite first-person pronoun used in business and respectful speech.

examples.text: わたくしが担当いたします。
わたくしはそのように考えます。

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Loanword from English 'salesman'.

examples.text: 彼は優秀なセールスマンです。
一人前のセールスマンになりたいです。
examples.trans: I want to become a full-fledged salesman.

meanings.note: Means both a fully qualified person and one serving of food.

examples.text: 早く一人前の仕事ができるようになりたいです。
examples.trans: I want to be able to do full-fledged work soon.

examples.text: ラーメンを一人前ください。

meanings.note: Read いちにち for duration/rate ('per day'); read ついたち for the 1st of the month.

examples.text: 一日十五分勉強します。
examples.trans: I study for fifteen minutes a day.

meanings.note: Combines 三 (three) with counter か月 (months).

examples.text: 日本に来て三か月になります。
examples.trans: It has been three months since I came to Japan.

examples.text: 三か月続けてみてください。
examples.trans: Please try continuing for three months.

meanings.note: Combines 三千 (3,000) with 円 (yen).

examples.text: 三千円お預かりします。

meanings.note: Refers to a person's life, career, and experiences.

examples.text: 人生を諦めないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't give up on life.

meanings.note: Used among friends and peers by men; switch to 私 or 僕 in formal settings.
Combines 十五 (15) with 分 (minutes).

examples.text: 駅まで歩いて十五分かかります。
examples.trans: It takes fifteen minutes on foot to the station.

examples.text: 十五分だけ待ってください。

meanings.en: be too cheap; be overly inexpensive
meanings.note: Compound ichidan verb from 安い (cheap) + すぎる (too much).

examples.text: この値段は安すぎます。
examples.trans: This price is way too cheap.

examples.text: 安すぎて少し心配です。
examples.trans: It's so cheap that I'm a little worried.

meanings.note: Used with が before it (ストーリーが必要だ 'a story is needed') or な before a noun.
Abstract noun formed from 必要 (necessary) + 性 (-ness).

examples.text: 英語の必要性を感じています。
examples.trans: I feel the need for English.

examples.text: 説明の必要性はありません。
examples.trans: There is no need for an explanation.

meanings.en: to think; to feel; to believe
meanings.note: Often follows quotative と to express an opinion or belief.

examples.text: それはいいと思います。

meanings.note: Compound noun meaning warm affection or devotion.

examples.text: 愛情を込めて作りました。
仕事に対する愛情が大切です。
examples.trans: Passion/love for your work is important.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb; takes を or と.

examples.text: 季節の変化を感じます。
examples.trans: I feel the change of seasons.

examples.text: 少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.

meanings.en: to teach; to tell; to show
meanings.note: Ichidan verb.
Read つき when meaning 'month' or 'moon'; read げつ in month names.

examples.text: 月三千円のサービスです。
今月は仕事が多いです。
examples.trans: There is a lot of work this month.

meanings.note: Combines 百 (100) with 円 (yen).

examples.text: 一日百円なら安いですね。
examples.trans: 100 yen a day is cheap, isn't it?

meanings.en: know; find out; be aware of
meanings.note: Godan verb; state of knowing is 知っている.

examples.text: 彼の電話番号を知っていますか。
examples.trans: Do you know his phone number?

examples.text: 本当の理由を知りたい。
examples.trans: I want to know the real reason.

meanings.note: Acknowledges that what the other person pointed out really is true.

examples.text: 確かにそのとおりですね。
確かに受け取りました。

meanings.note: Transitive ichidan verb.

examples.text: 毎日運動を続けています。
三か月続けてみてください。
examples.trans: Please try keeping it up for three months.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: もう少しよく考えてみます。
examples.trans: I'll think about it a little more carefully.

meanings.note: Compound noun.

examples.text: 毎週英会話の教室に通っています。
examples.trans: I attend an English conversation class every week.

examples.text: 英会話の教材を探しています。
examples.trans: I'm looking for English conversation study materials.

meanings.note: Ichidan verb.

examples.text: 最後まで諦めないでください。
examples.trans: Please don't give up until the end.

examples.text: 夢を諦めたくありません。
examples.trans: I don't want to give up on my dream.

meanings.note: I-adjective meaning expensive (price) or high/tall.

examples.text: この時計はとても高いです。
少し高いと感じるかもしれません。
examples.trans: You may feel it's a little expensive.
